label: early original-phase l/r/n/i/g/x after a u/p/q/k/b/3/v/a/m-heavy prefix
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (98% of mass), firing at positions 1-4 (t=2,3 hold ~80% of mass; never t=0, almost never t>=5). It needs the current input to be one of l, r, n, i, g, x (l strongest at 8.5x lift, then r, n, i, g, x; s weakly), usually a first occurrence, AND a prefix made mostly of tokens from {u,p,q,k,b,3,v,a,m}. The strongest activations are sequences like k u a [l], u p a [l], k q a [l]: two of u/k/p/q then a, then l. The trigger tokens with no such prefix (e.g. 0 n, c 1 p k l) mostly stay silent, so it acts like a soft weighted sum over prefix tokens rather than a clean rule. That is why precision tops out around 0.4. Weak residual firing: on <DEL> right after such a prefix, and at the first copy-phase steps (outputting u/k). Does not fire on most other input tokens (a, f, y, digits) or in the copy phase generally.
